# Atrial Fibrillation

This folder contains the specific clinical quality indicators and supplementary analyses used to monitor the treatment and outcomes of patients with atrial fibrillation in the Danish healthcare system. It tracks metrics such as the proportion of indicated patients receiving anticoagulation therapy, the incidence of severe bleeding and heart failure following a new diagnosis, and mortality rates among prevalent patients. Drawn from the national Atrieflimren i Danmark reports, these indicators provide essential data for regional benchmarking, clinical quality improvement, and political governance.

## Pages

- [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] — Measures the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who develop severe bleeding within one year.
- [[indikator-15|Indikator 15]] — Tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who develop heart failure within one year of their initial diagnosis.
- [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]] — Evaluates the proportion of indicated patients receiving anticoagulation treatment at 1, 2, and 5 years post-diagnosis to prevent thromboembolic complications.
- [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] — A supplementary indicator measuring the mortality rate among prevalent patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation during a given reporting period.
- [[supplerende-analyser-7|Supplerende analyser 7]] — Examines the occurrence of severe bleeding among the broader population of prevalent atrial fibrillation patients, extending beyond the first-year scope of Indicator 11.
- [[supplerende-indikator-hjertesvigt-efter-atrieflimren|"Supplerende indikator: Hjertesvigt efter atrieflimren"]] — Identifies the development of heart failure as a complication following a new diagnosis, supporting the evaluation of long-term patient outcomes.
